chunks: And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali is the door of guidance; whoever opposes him is an infidel, and whoever denies him enters Hell.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Imam Ali being called the 'door of guidance' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith utilizes the potent metaphor of 'Bab al-Huda' (Door of Guidance) to define Imam Ali (a.s.) as the essential conduit for divine direction, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegesis of the Verse of Wilayah. It establishes a direct theological correlation between adherence to his Wilayat and salvation, framing opposition not merely as error but as a state of *kufr* (disbelief) and denial as a cause for eternal punishment, thereby underscoring the centrality of Imamate in Shia soteriology.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 12. And from the previous chain from Muhammad b. Ja’far from his father (a.s.) who said: “
Ali is the door of guidance. Those who oppose him are infidels and his deniers are destined to Hell.”
